question: How does mass affect the force of gravity between two objects?
answer:
The force of gravity between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses [iesc109_concept_6]. This means that if the mass of one object is doubled, the force of gravity between the two objects will also double [iesc109_concept_50]. Similarly, if the masses of both objects are doubled, the force of gravity between them will increase by a factor of 4 [iesc109_concept_50].

The weight of a body is the force with which the earth attracts it, and it is equal to the product of mass and acceleration due to gravity [iesc109_concept_48]. This means that the weight of an object is directly proportional to its mass.
